findings.title: Omission of secret masking on history read command views
findings.requirement_ref: phase-100368 §7 (Security Constraints - Required Controls & Sensitive Data Rules), AC-100368-04, NFR-6
findings.recommendation: In `HistoryGroup::decorate` (`crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read_history.rs`), invoke `clio_config::secret::mask_value("", payload)` so that any credential or secret material embedded within task records, definitions, failure lessons, or temporal records is masked in CLI output per §7.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED (round 2; round-1 regression fixed). Round 1 masked every history payload with `clio_config::secret::mask_value`, which rewrites non-string leaves: `failure list` emitted the non-secret integer `FailureRecord.lesson_tokens` (clio-types/src/history.rs:233) as `"[REDACTED]"`, breaking the MCP-parity contract (AC-100368-02). Round 2 replaces that call with a new type-preserving helper `clio_config::secret::mask_string_secrets` (crates/clio-config/src/secret.rs), which masks only secret-keyed string leaves and leaves non-string leaves untouched, plus the existing `scrub_prose_secrets` prose pass over every string leaf. `HistoryGroup::decorate` (crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read_history.rs:84) now calls `mask_string_secrets("", payload)` + `scrub_prose_secrets(payload)`; `WorkspaceGroup::decorate` (crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read_workspace.rs:71) uses the same helper for `audit trail` (same §7 control, same regression class). Evidence: new test `cli_read_history_tests::failure_list_preserves_mcp_structured_fields` asserts the CLI `failures` array equals the raw `failures_for_task` tool result and that `lesson_tokens` stays numeric; new `secret_tests::mask_string_secrets_masks_strings_and_keeps_non_strings` and a workspace numeric assertion cover the helper; `history_views_mask_planted_secrets` still masks planted definition/lesson secrets. Out-of-tree probe on the exact failure payload: old `mask_value` -> `"lesson_tokens":"[REDACTED]"`; new pass -> `"lesson_tokens":3` with `lesson: password=****cret`. `make check` EXIT=0; `make coverage` EXIT=0, 292 files checked, TOTAL lines 97.96% functions 98.96%, all files >=90% (secret.rs 100/100, cli_read_history.rs 98.36/100, cli_read_workspace.rs 100/100). Boundary (unchanged, non-blocking): `scrub_inline_secrets` scrubs `key: secret` / `key=secret` prose but not JSON-quoted `"key": "secret"` text embedded inside a definition/lesson; the key-name mask applies only to structured string fields.

findings.title: Missing tool binding arrow for `graph query` in top-level `print_help()`
findings.recommendation: Update `crates/clio-lib/src/main.rs:401` in `print_help()` to append `-> graph_query`, matching the formatting of all other 19 CLI read command entries.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED as recommended. The line now reads `clio graph query SEED_ID [--max-hops N] [--edge-type coactivation|explicit] -> graph_query`. Additionally, the top-level help text was extracted into `help_text()` and a new drift test (`main_read_tests::top_level_help_binds_every_read_command_tool`) asserts every `command_bindings()` entry appears in the help with its `-> <tool>` arrow (two-tool lines via ` / `), so this formatting drift cannot recur silently. Evidence: the new test passes; `cargo test -p clio --bin clio` → 293 passed, 0 failed; `make check` EXIT=0; `make coverage` EXIT=0 with main.rs at 93.78% lines / 100.0% functions.

plan_unlimited: Centralized masking pass in `cli_read::run_parsed` — DISAGREED by evidence, not implemented. The masking heuristics are substring-based over field names (`clio-config/src/secret.rs`: SECRET_MARKERS contains `auth`, `path_is_secret` uses `contains`), so a blanket pass over all 20 read views would redact legitimate fields — e.g. any `author` field matches the `auth` marker — corrupting `get`/`show`/`recall` output. Phase §7 scopes masking to audit/history views, tool handlers already mask at their own boundary (`read_tools.rs:222` inspect, `runtime_index.rs:131`, hygiene/sync tools), and the per-view `decorate` mask matches the established `WorkspaceGroup` pattern. The scoped F-01 fix covers the required surface without that blast radius. ROUND 2: still DISAGREED, now with direct evidence. The `auth`/`token` substring heuristics do over-match domain payloads: the round-1 per-view blanket `mask_value` proved it by rewriting the non-secret integer `lesson_tokens` to a string. The round-2 fix therefore refined the per-view mask to `mask_string_secrets` (type-preserving) instead of centralizing a blanket pass, which would have spread the same false-positive class to all 20 read views.

`render_persona` UX enhancement (render key names/preview entries instead of counts) -> DISAGREED, not implemented. The view output is pinned by contract: `cli_read_graph_tests.rs:170-175` asserts the exact string `stable: 1
preferences: 1
dropped_keys: 1`, and the phase contract requires commands to 'return the same structured results as their MCP counterparts' (§1 Expected Outcome). Changing the human view is a UX feature request with no owning requirement; implementing it would break the pinned view contract and AC evidence without authorization.

Automated tests verifying every `command_bindings()` entry has an exact corresponding line in `print_help()` with the `-> <tool>` pattern -> DONE (see F-02 resolution): `main_read_tests::top_level_help_binds_every_read_command_tool` iterates all 20 bindings against the extracted `help_text()`.
